html:
Polish priest, born Karol Wojtyła in 1920, who was pope from 1978 to 2005. He was the first pope who was not Italian in 455 years.

He grew up in a small town near Kraków. Under Nazi occupation he studied for the priesthood in secret. Under communist rule he rose to become Archbishop of Kraków and took part in the Second Vatican Council.

Elected pope in October 1978, he made his first visit home in June 1979. Huge crowds came to his open air masses, and his message, "Be not afraid", gave Poles new confidence. A year later the Solidarity movement was born, and he is widely seen as helping inspire the peaceful end of communism in Poland in 1989.

He survived being shot in Saint Peter's Square in 1981 and later visited and forgave his attacker. He held firm conservative views on doctrine, sex and the role of women, and he apologised for past wrongs of the church, including toward Jews. He died in 2005 and was declared a saint in 2014 by Pope Francis.
sum: Polish priest, born Karol Wojtyła in 1920, who was pope from 1978 to 2005. He was the first pope who was not Italian in 455 years.
